response: No, sugars-free medicines are not more erosive than sugars-containing medicines. In fact, sugars-free medicines are generally considered to be less erosive because they do not contain fermentable carbohydrates that can contribute to tooth decay and erosion. However, some sugars-free medicines may contain acidic ingredients, such as citric acid or tartaric acid, that can still pose a risk of erosion, especially if taken frequently or in large quantities.
